title: How an mRNA Vaccine Works

segments.say: Most vaccines show your body a piece of the germ. An mRNA vaccine does something cleverer: it gives your body the recipe.

anim.title: The recipe
items: mRNA: an instruction for one protein
Wrapped in a tiny bubble of fat

segments.say: mRNA is a short instruction for making one protein. Wrapped in a tiny bubble of fat, it slips into your cells, and they make that protein, say, the spike of a virus.

anim.title: The training
items: It makes antibodies and memory cells

segments.say: Your immune system sees the strange protein, makes antibodies, and remembers it. When the real virus comes, it is ready.
The mRNA never enters the nucleus, where your DNA is kept, and it can't change your DNA. Your cells break it down within days.

left.title: Older vaccines
items: Grow the germ or its parts

right.title: mRNA
items: Change it quickly for new strains

segments.say: Why so fast during COVID? Because once the virus's code is known, the recipe can be written and changed quickly. The work behind it won the twenty twenty-three Nobel Prize in Medicine.
India's first mRNA vaccine, GEMCOVAC, was cleared for emergency use in twenty twenty-two, and can be kept in an ordinary fridge.
For Prelims: mRNA carries the recipe, cells make the protein, the body remembers, and your DNA stays untouched.

sources: US CDC, 'Understanding How COVID-19 Vaccines Work' / 'mRNA vaccines': mRNA instructs cells to make a harmless piece of spike protein; it never enters the nucleus and does not affect DNA; cells break down the mRNA soon after
NobelPrize.org, Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2023: awarded for nucleoside base modification discoveries that enabled effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19
PIB / Department of Biotechnology, June 2022: GEMCOVAC-19, India's first mRNA vaccine, developed with DBT support, received emergency use authorisation; stored at 2–8°C

quiz.q: What does an mRNA vaccine give your cells?
quiz.why: It carries the recipe; your cells make the protein.

options: No; it never enters the nucleus and breaks down
quiz.why: It stays outside the nucleus and is broken down within days.

reviewNote: Facts were read against CDC's mRNA explainer, NobelPrize.org and the DBT/PIB release on GEMCOVAC. No people named or shown. Moving facts: none.
